messages:
sam: quick handoff — I'm on until 22:00 UTC, leaving a short watchlist. Not an incident, but please keep an eye and escalate if anything degrades further.

sam: Observed items: 1) encoder-pool error rate up ~2% over baseline last 40m (p95 latency stable but p50 noisy). 2) eu-1 prefetch queue pressure hitting 75-85% intermittently during traffic bursts (short spikes, resolves). 3) noisy alert 'encoder-latency-spike' firing on p50; looks correlated with batch scheduling churn.

sam: Actions I already did: bumped encoder pool retry backoff to 200ms for this cycle, disabled the low-severity encoder-latency alert on the staging rule (not prod), and opened a ticket (INC-4572) to investigate scheduling jitter.

marta: taking over from sam, thanks. noted the queue pressure — do we have a temporary mitigation if eu-1 spikes into sustained >90%?

sam: matters: not full mitigation yet. Short-term options: 1) shift some low-priority routing to eu-2 (can toggle via routing-policy -> traffic-split). 2) enable brief burst capacity (dedicated) for eu-1 (costly). I left the routing-split at 90/10 eu1/eu2 to avoid churn.

alex: FYI I added a dashboard panel called "prefetch queue pressure (eu-1)" and a simple alert that triggers only if >90% for 3m to reduce noise. link: https://redwood.dashboards/prefetch-eu1

taylor: thanks. i'm going to submit a tiny alert rule tweak: increase encoder-latency-spike severity to medium and require 2/3 windows before firing. I'll open a PR and tag you @marta for review.

marta: please do. also ping me if any autoscale policies kick — we saw weird delays with cooldown set to 30s last week.

oncall-bot: reminder — runbook for encoding/queue issues: https://runbooks.internal/encoding-queue. Use the `fallback-to-cpu` flow if GPU pool becomes saturated.

marta: noted runbook. two quick asks before i fully swap: 1) sam, any recent deploys touching encoder scheduler? 2) alex, can you keep an eye on any node drains in eu-1 (k8s events)?

sam: no deploys targeting scheduler in the last 12h. last deploy was a small cache TTL change.

alex: will watch nodes and post if kubectl shows drain events. set a short watch on k8s-event stream.

marta: great. i'll be primary until 06:00 UTC. if anything starts trending (encoder errors >5% OR queue pressure >90% sustained), escalate to eng-sre and call the oncall rota.

taylor: added the PR for alert tweak: https://git.internal/redwood/alerts/pull/322 — @marta please quick review, should reduce noise without hiding real regressions.

sam: thanks all. leaving a couple TODOs in the ticket: - add a golden prompt set to repro jitter - check kernel selection logs on the affected GPUs - consider temporary routing policy to divert non-critical traffic.

marta: copy. i'll follow up in the morning with notes and any further mitigations. handing off now — @taylor you have my slack DM if you need fast approvals. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: shift change logged: sam -> marta at 1766000483. If you need to escalate, use /escalate and include incident commander.
